newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-MONACO TEST NEW RESOLVE AT FORTRESS LILLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MONACO TEST NEW RESOLVE AT FORTRESS LILLE.

text.p: Monaco ran riot in Germany and again on their own shores last week but the northern French outpost of Lille, so far impregnable this season, may prove a tougher proposition in their first division sortie on Friday.

Monaco, having shocked Borussia Moenchengladbach 4-2 in the away leg of their UEFA Cup second round tie, romped to a 4-1 home win over Nice last Saturday that put them in second place, six points behind leaders Paris Saint-Germain.
Lille are unbeaten in seven matches at home and four in a row including their first away victory at Montpellier last weekend.
But their pragmatic coach Jean-Michel Cavalli says modest Lille's objective this season is still to ensure survival in the top flight in a season which will end with four sides relegated.
"We're keeping our feet on the ground, there's no question of getting carried away," Cavalli said.

But Cavalli, for whom eight-goal Yugoslav striker Miladin Becanovic and promising 20-year-old Djezon Boutoille return from suspension, is not about to shut up shop against the second best attack in the division with 22 goals in 13 games.

"We have nothing to lose, we're ahead of our predictions (for the season). We're not going to close up the game as a matter of respect to our spectators, who are coming to the ground in ever increasing numbers," Cavalli said.
His opposite number Jean Tigana will not contemplate anything other than a victory for a Monaco side that on paper is the best in the French first division but has only lately come into form.
Brazilian Anderson, who has scored seven goals in the league this season, and Victor Ikpeba of Nigeria are on song up front with two and four goals apiece in the heady last 10 days.

"This is a match to be won. We're well prepared and Lille are just behind us in the standings, they're something of a surprise and this will be another good test," said Tigana, who fears PSG pulling further ahead if they win at Rennes.
Monaco are still without injured midfield general Enzo Scifo but welcome back Algerian Ali Benarbia from suspension.
Benarbia said: "We must go there (to Lille) with the same state of mind that spurred us at Bastia and in Germany."
A tenacious performance in a 0-0 draw in the tough away fixture at Bastia two weekends ago was the launching pad for Monaco's subsequent successes.
